rows.selection_reason: No experiments are complete, so the main uncertainty is whether a simple unimodal representation provides a useful validation-accuracy baseline before adding multiprofile aggregation, learned encoders, or fusion. config_001 tests RNA-only, single-profile PCA, isolating the RNA representation without aggregation or fusion. It is the best next use of budget because it is a minimal, low-confound reference point: it calibrates performance, reveals whether RNA signal is present, and creates an anchor for later comparisons of multiprofile aggregation, learned RNA encoders, image-only models, and multimodal fusion.

Existing evidence is sparse: only config_001, an RNA-only singleprofile PCA baseline, has been tested, with moderate validation accuracy 0.485 and F1 0.464. This leaves major uncertainty about whether image features provide useful signal. config_010 tests an image-only singleprofile ResNet50 baseline, isolating the image representation without adding aggregation or fusion. This is the best next experiment because it establishes a necessary unimodal image reference, reducing uncertainty about modality before investing in more complex multimodal or multiprofile configurations.

The existing evidence shows RNA-only PCA singleprofile is much stronger than image-only ResNet singleprofile (48.5% vs 20.8% validation accuracy), but it is still unclear whether using multiple profiles adds useful signal or whether simple aggregation is sufficient. config_002 keeps the proven PCA RNA representation and changes only the profile setting to multiprofile with avgpool, directly testing the effect of multiprofile aggregation. Under a limited budget, this is a focused, low-risk extension of the current best direction and avoids confounding changes in modality, RNA encoder, or fusion.

The strongest result so far is config_002, where multiprofile RNA with PCA and avgpool reaches 0.591 accuracy, clearly above single-profile RNA (0.485) and far above image-only ResNet50 (0.208). This suggests multiprofile RNA is promising, but it is still unclear whether transformer aggregation can improve over avgpool. config_003 changes only the aggregation method from avgpool to transformer while keeping the same RNA encoder and multiprofile setting, so it directly isolates the effect of aggregation. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the most promising direction, reduces uncertainty about a key design choice, and establishes a stronger RNA-only baseline before testing more complex multimodal fusion.

RNA multiprofile avgpool (config_002) is the clear best so far, while image-only ResNet singleprofile (config_010) is weak. The key uncertainty is whether the multiprofile+avgpool benefit transfers to the image modality or whether image is intrinsically weak. config_011 tests image-only with the same multiprofile+avgpool setting and the same ResNet50 encoder, isolating profile/aggregation effects without introducing fusion. This is a simple, high-information gate before multimodal experiments: if image improves, ResNet+avgpool multimodal configs become promising; if not, budget should shift to RNA representation rather than fusion.

The strongest evidence so far is that RNA-only multiprofile with avgpool and PCA is much better than single-profile RNA or transformer aggregation, while ResNet image-only multiprofile avgpool remains weak. The key uncertainty is whether fusing the weak image modality with the strong RNA modality helps at all. config_018 keeps the best RNA setting and the already characterized ResNet image setting fixed, adding only multimodal concat fusion. This is the simplest direct test of whether multimodal fusion can improve on the current best unimodal baseline, making it a high-value use of the next limited experiment.

The best completed experiment is config_018, a multimodal multiprofile PCA+ResNet model with avgpool and concat fusion, but only concat fusion has been tested in this strong setting. config_019 keeps the same RNA encoder, profile setting, image encoder, and aggregation, changing only fusion to weighted, so it cleanly isolates the effect of fusion. This is a direct exploitation of the current most promising direction while reducing uncertainty about whether adaptive fusion can improve the modest gain from adding image features.

The current best evidence is that multiprofile PCA RNA with ResNet50 image features, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion is the strongest setting (config_019, 0.639), but image-only performance is weak and only ResNet50 has been tested as the image encoder. config_025 changes only the image encoder to imagenet_vit_l while keeping the best profile, RNA encoder, aggregation, and fusion, so it cleanly tests whether a stronger image representation can improve the promising multimodal pipeline. This is a high-value exploitation step: it may directly improve the best configuration and also clarifies whether further gains should come from image representation under the current best design.

The strongest result so far is config_019, a multimodal multiprofile model using PCA, ResNet, avgpool, and weighted fusion with validation accuracy 0.639 and F1 0.620. The main unresolved uncertainty is RNA representation, since only PCA has been tested, while the current best fusion, aggregation, profile, and image settings are already relatively well supported. config_031 changes only the RNA encoder from PCA to scvi_n200 while keeping the known-good multimodal multiprofile, avgpool, weighted-fusion, and ResNet configuration. This will clarify whether a learned RNA encoder can improve the best current direction or whether PCA is already sufficient. It is the best next experiment because it exploits the strongest known configuration while testing a major representation decision in a single-factor comparison.

The strongest completed configuration is config_031 (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted, resnet50) with 0.6776 accuracy and 0.6464 F1, showing that the scvi RNA representation plus multiprofile avgpool and weighted fusion is a promising direction. The key remaining uncertainty in this branch is whether the image encoder should remain resnet50 or be replaced by imagenet_vit_l; under PCA, resnet50 and ViT were nearly tied (0.6390 vs 0.6352), so the image representation effect is unresolved and may interact differently with the stronger scvi RNA encoder. config_037 changes only the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l while keeping the best-performing scvi/multiprofile/avgpool/weighted setup, isolating the image representation effect. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the current best direction, has high expected performance, and efficiently clarifies whether a stronger pretrained image encoder can improve the best configuration or whether resnet50 is already sufficient.
